industry.ipm: Indian domestic formulations market (IPM) ₹2,565 bn in FY26, +9.9% (IQVIA, as cited in Mankind Pharma's AR FY26 industry section, published 9-Jul-2026)
industry.ipmGrowth: IPM +8.9% in Q3FY26 (acute +6.9%, chronic +12%; Ipca +10.6%, acute +8.4%, chronic +15%); in Q1FY27 Ipca +11.7% on IQVIA with chronic +17.2% vs the market's 15.2% and acute +8.9% vs 4.5% (Ipca Q3FY26 and Q1FY27 calls)
industry.pricing: Price rises on NLEM/DPCO-scheduled drugs follow the wholesale price index; non-scheduled drugs may rise up to 10% a year. Ipca takes 5-6% a year and planned 6-7% for FY27 to offset input costs (Q4FY26 call)
industry.chronicShift: Growth is shifting to chronic therapies (cardiac, diabetes, CNS, urology); Ipca's chronic segments grew 15-17% in FY26-Q1FY27 against 12-15% for the market
industry.glp1: Semaglutide's Indian patent expired in Mar-2026 and many companies launched; Ipca was not in the first wave and is looking to in-license a GLP-1 (Q3FY26 call, 16-Feb-2026)
industry.antimalarials: Domestic anti-malarials fell 21-24% a quarter through FY26-Q1FY27 and are now ~1-2% of Ipca's domestic sales; the global institutional anti-malarial market depends on donor funding (Global Fund and others), which tightened in FY26 (Q4FY26 call: 'funding constraints')
industry.usGenerics: US generics: price erosion in old products, shortages and onshoring pressure; Indian plants with clean USFDA status are scarce assets

strengths: Pain and rheumatology franchise: 53% of domestic sales; Zerodol family (aceclofenac), HCQS (hydroxychloroquine), Folitrax (methotrexate) are among the country's top brands; top 10 brands ₹2,135 cr, 38% of IQVIA sales (Jul-2026)
Backward integration: Ipca makes most of its own APIs (80 APIs, 62 EDQM certificates), so material cost is ~25% of standalone sales and gross margin ~71% consolidated
Diversification few Indian mid-caps have: India branded, emerging-market branded with own field forces (Africa, CIS, Asia, LatAm), regulated-market generics (UK/EU, Australia/NZ, Canada, US) and APIs
Clean regulatory status again: Ratlam, Pithampur and Silvassa VAI and out of import alert since FY24; Tarapur VAI in Feb-2026
A conservative, promoter-run balance sheet: net cash, low payout, debt from the Unichem deal repaid within three years
weaknesses: Mid-sized in India: rank 16 with a 2.08% share; little presence in the fastest-growing new categories (GLP-1s, specialty biologics)
Concentration in pain: one therapy is over half the domestic business and several large brands are price-controlled
Institutional anti-malarials and APIs are cyclical and tender- or price-driven (FY23: EPS −47%)
Unichem: a sub-scale US generics business (8% margin in FY26) bought at the top of Ipca's own cycle; integration benefits are slow
Working capital is heavy (~144 days) and capex is high for a branded company
moat.verdict: A narrow moat: real in India pain/rheumatology and in cost (API integration), not in pricing power or innovation.

critiques: Bull: the margin story is only half done. Standalone margin went from ~22.7% (FY25) to 26% in Q1FY27 and management sees 30%; Unichem from 8% to 11% with 13% guided and mid-teens possible. Each point is ~₹3.5 of EPS.

Bull: the US is finally open for Ipca's own products (import alerts lifted in FY24; Unichem USA sells them): Ipca's products drove Unichem's US +27% in Q1FY27, with 7-8 launches a year across the two.

Bear: Q1FY27 flattered: ~5pp of the 21% growth was the weak rupee, ₹40 cr was delayed institutional shipments and ₹32 cr of forex gains sat in EBITDA on Screener's basis. Strip those and underlying growth was ~14% with a ~22.9% margin.

Bear: freight (2-3x on some lanes), solvents (+40-50%) and packaging costs rose sharply from Feb-2026 with the West Asia conflict; management says price rises offset them, but generics contracts reprice slowly.

Bear: capital allocation has been mixed: Unichem (₹1,543 cr for 52.67%, still earning ~8-11% margins), Krebs (₹130 cr impaired, now being merged in), Lyka (loss-making JV). The ₹42.7 cr paid to four whole-time directors is 3.7% of profit.
Bear: the stock trades at ~28x our FY28E EPS after a ~47% rise in twelve months; the street's post-Q1 targets cluster at ₹1,935-2,190, only 0-14% above the 30-Sep price.
gaps: Kotak, Jefferies, Morgan Stanley, Nirmal Bang, Nomura, JM Financial and Nuvama notes before 30-Sep-2026 could not be read in full; only targets (and for JM/Nuvama the thesis) are known. Axis Capital's Sell (29-May-2026) may have been revised after Q1FY27 (not found).
Segment profitability is not disclosed (no EBITDA by business). Our split (Ipca ex-Unichem ~25.5-26%, Unichem ~12.5%) rests on management's call comments.

Unichem's profit as consolidated by Ipca (after the 2023 fair-value adjustments) is not disclosed; our minorities forecast uses estimates (₹130-225 cr) cross-checked against reported minorities (FY26 ₹42.7 cr; Q1FY27 ~₹21 cr).
The quarterly split of export formulations into branded / generic / institutional is available only for some quarters (Q1FY26, Q4FY26, Q1FY27; nine-month totals).

The exact USFDA EIR date for the Ratlam and Silvassa plants and the date the import alerts were formally removed are not in the filings we read (AR FY24 says they were lifted during FY24; SEZ Indore's EIR was reported in Oct-2023).
